name: Pitbull
manufacturer: Originally developed for Shelf gang enforcers; currently produced by multiple cooks, most notably a Shelf operation called 'the Kennel'
description: A crude but effective combat stimulant combining stolen epinephrine, a synthetic testosterone analogue cooked from industrial precursors, and a pain-suppressing compound derived from repurposed veterinary analgesics. Designed explicitly to make people fight harder and feel less — and it works. Users experience dramatically reduced pain response and heightened aggression for a focused window of time.
effects: aggressive confidence and reduced fear response
significant physical performance enhancement — strength and speed
tunnel-vision focus on immediate physical task
side_effects: cardiac stress during use — multiple documented heart attacks in users over 35
post-dose crash involves extreme pain as suppression wears off
psychological aggression persisting hours after dose
chronic use causes adrenal fatigue and hormonal disruption
users have sustained serious injuries without awareness during intoxication
cultural_context: Pitbull is the drug of Shelf violence — used by gang enforcers, underground fighters, and desperate people in dangerous situations. It has a reputation for making users dangerous beyond their normal capability, which is both the appeal and the terror. Shelf communities have mixed feelings: it's the reason certain people can protect their block, and it's the reason certain people become uncontrollable. Some users take it knowing they'll pay for the pain later, and do it anyway.
story_hooks: A Shelf enforcer on Pitbull killed three people including a bystander — now their gang is being pressured to hand them over, but the enforcer claims they don't remember it
Someone has been supplying Pitbull to increasingly young Shelf residents, and the source traces back to a gang that's deliberately destabilizing a district
An underground fight circuit has banned Pitbull after several deaths — but the ban is impossible to enforce, and a fixer needs to navigate the politics of Shelf combat sports
